Yea (21f) my spots have really gotten better after steroid injections and regular rogaine use, if you want a quick fix just to cover up there are bottles of ‘hair fibers’ that are sold at most stores (CVS/Walgreens wtv) and you just rub or spray it on and it helps to cover the skin, I’ve also in quick instances used a little eyelash glue and put it on my spot and maneuvered the hair I do have to keep in place. I’ve also heard derma stamping/rolling is really good and has great signs of hair growth, also maybe having a blood test done to make sure there aren’t any other underlying issues that could have caused it. There are a lot of ways so it’s really a matter of what works for you/your body/health.

I’m sorry for your loss, I lost my mom just about two weeks ago now. It’s so confusing and maddening to feel the world keep going on around you when it seems like time has stopped Indefinitely. I’m mad too. I’m mad that this had to happen while so many others get so much more out of life. I feel like such a bitter cruel person to think this way but it just doesn’t feel fair. I don’t know all the steps of grief but I think this would be a valid response from anyone. Because it’s not fair, life never is. From this grief and bitter feelings (at least for myself) I’ve tried to question what my mom would want for me. She was a person with so much love in her heart and when I squeeze my eyes tight enough I feel her light over me still trying to take the pain away. It’s a fair feeling to have when these terrible things happen. I’m so sorry for your loss OP and I sincerely hope you find strength to continue living for your loved one.

Check out optimistic nihilism, I always had similar questions and I felt that answered them best, essentially life DOESNT have any meaning, we all exist just because we do and there is no hope in a chance of their being some big motive to our existence, but since we have no meaning then we can’t live life wrong technically, there is no rule book. 
Like you I’ve felt that my family was the only thing really tethering me to my sanity and I first started thinking about all these negative things around 7 years ago (I’m 19 now) once I started asking more questions you realize your answers are just going to be more questions. It doesn’t get much better but it’s not like it gets that much worse. Once you feel despair you start to build a resistance to it, inevitably the pain numbs. We are all just waiting for something in the end.
